To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of Quantile Normalization and Cubic-Splines Normalization is recommended in metabolomic studies, (ii) these normalization methods are able to reduce the variance in the data, and (iii) they are able to reduce unwanted bias and to improve sample classification.
Quantile and Cubicspline Normalization performed best in terms of removing bias and accurately detecting fold changes.

the use of Quantile Normalization and Cubic-Spine Normalization in combination with the Pareto scaling and the variance stabilizing transformation, respectively, is recommended for NMR-based metabolomics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic comparison of different data normalization methods in metabolomic analysis.
the systematic evaluation of preprocessing methods for NMR metabolomics data.
improving the quality of NMR-based metabolomics data by applying state-of-the art data preprocessing methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Quantile Normalization is the best choice in terms of sample classification, while Cubic-Spline and Variance Stabilization are the most appropriate for screening for differentially expressed metabolites.
the use of Quantile Normalization and Cubic-Splines Normalization is highly recommended for NMR metabolomic data analysis.
Quantile and Cubicspline Normalization should be used in NMR-based metabolomics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of the preprocessing method is highly dependent on the type of data and the analysis goal.
Quantile Normalization, which is a simple method to reduce bias and variance, is the most suitable preprocessing method for metabolomic data analysis.
Quantile normalization should be used in NMR metabolomic data preprocessing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data preprocessing methods developed for other omic technologies can be successfully applied to NMR-based metabolomics.
the choice of normalization method is critical to the outcome of metabolomic analysis.
, in order to achieve optimal results, the choice of a normalization method should be based on the experimental design of the metabolomics study.
